text:
Sean Gallagher: Kicking off SRE requirements for Safe apply + rollback. Need to lock down operational SLOs + MTTR targets + what we page on (failed/stuck applies). Please comment with what you want to hold teams to.

Neha Kapoor: +1. We need something we can confidently tell enterprise: “rollback in minutes” isn’t a slogan, it’s an SLO.

Rafael Mendes: From on-call POV:
- If Optimize config change is bad, I want rollback available fast + the UI/API to be unambiguous.
- Also need alerts that are *actionable* (not “some deploy happened”).

Allison Grant: For instrumentation, we should standardize metrics naming + labels now so dashboards/alerts aren’t a mess later. I’m assuming we’ll have correlation ids per apply.

Sean Gallagher: Proposed starting point (open to edits):

SLOs (prod):
1) Apply initiation (control plane acceptance): p99 < 2s for /apply + /rollback endpoints.
2) Apply completion (scope reaches “Applied”): 99% < 10 min, 99.9% < 20 min.
3) Rollback completion: 99% < 5 min, 99.9% < 10 min.
4) “Stuck rollout” detection: detect within 3 min (so on-call isn’t discovering via customer complaints).

MTTR target for config regressions:
- Detect + initiate rollback < 10 min (p95) once alert fires.

Alerting:
- Page if rollback fails or if apply is stuck.
- Ticket if apply failure rate is elevated but auto-retries resolve.

Thoughts?

Aisha Bello: 10 min for apply completion feels fine for large scopes, but rollback should be tighter if we’re using it to mitigate incidents.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. During incidents, “rollback in 5 min 99%” is the difference between Sev2 and Sev1.

Neha Kapoor: Can we push rollback to 99% < 3 min for Hosted + Dedicated? Private might be slower depending on customer infra.

Allison Grant: Suggest we define SLOs per deployment mode:
- Hosted (Redwood-managed): most strict
- Dedicated: strict but dependent on cluster size
- Private: best effort with clear caveats, but still must have determinism + audit logs

Sean Gallagher: Good call. Let’s split:

Hosted/Dedicated (prod):
- Rollback completion 99% < 3 min, 99.9% < 7 min.
- Apply completion 99% < 10 min, 99.9% < 20 min.

Private:
- Rollback completion target 99% < 10 min (operator-run), but must provide progress + reason when blocked (connectivity, paused agent, etc).

Aisha Bello: On alerts, I want explicit states:
- APPLYING
- APPLIED
- FAILED
- ROLLING_BACK
- ROLLED_BACK
- ROLLBACK_FAILED
- STUCK (derived)

We should page on STUCK and *_FAILED in prod.

Allison Grant: +1. Also for “stuck” we should distinguish “no progress” vs “partial progress” (split brain risk). Partial is higher severity.

Tomáš Novák: +1 on split brain. Can we define a hard invariant? e.g., within a given scope, runtime should never serve mixed configs beyond some short convergence window.

Sean Gallagher: We can put an operational invariant:
- Convergence window: <= 2 minutes where nodes may be on N or N-1, but control plane must show progress.
- If >2 minutes with mixed versions => page.

Rafael Mendes: That’s exactly what I need. When I’m on-call, I want “mixed versions >2m” to scream at me.

Devon Price: From incident tooling side: if we emit a single “config_change_id”, incident-bot can post:
- what changed (diff summary)
- scope (customer/region/cluster)
- link to rollback button
- current status (applying/applied/stuck)

We should standardize payload now.

Sean Gallagher: Nice. Re: alert thresholds, proposal:

Metrics (names tbd, but behavior matters):
- optimize_config_apply_duration_seconds{env,mode,scope_type}
- optimize_config_rollback_duration_seconds{...}
- optimize_config_change_state{state=...}
- optimize_config_propagation_progress{applied_nodes,total_nodes}
- optimize_config_change_attempts_total{result=success|failure, action=apply|rollback}

Alerts (prod):
P1 (page):
- Any rollback action in prod ends in ROLLBACK_FAILED.
- Any config change stuck > 5 min (no progress in progress metric).
- Mixed versions (applied_nodes between 0 and total_nodes) persists > 2 min.

P2 (page):
- Apply failed for enterprise tenant (Dedicated/Private) OR for Hosted “shared critical routes”.

Ticket:
- apply_attempt failure rate > 2% over 30 min (if retries succeed).
- apply_duration p99 > 15 min for 1h.

Aisha Bello: 5 min “stuck” might be too long if rollback is our mitigation. I’d rather:
- Warn at 2 min no-progress
- Page at 4 min no-progress

Allison Grant: +1 to two-stage (warning->page). Also add a “control plane accepted but runtime never started” category (webhook/queue failures).

Neha Kapoor: Agree. Also: we should *not* page for canary gate failures if system automatically stops and leaves prior version serving. That’s expected behavior.

Sean Gallagher: Great point. So:
- If canary gate blocks apply and system auto-aborts cleanly => no page, emit event + ticket.
- If canary gate blocks but rollout continues anyway (bug) => page.

Rafael Mendes: Also include this in runbook: “gate blocked” is not incident unless customer impact.

Tomáš Novák: For MTTR, I want a firm target:
- Config regression MTTR (customer-visible latency/error spike) <= 15 min p95 for Hosted, assuming on-call acknowledges within 5 min.

Sean Gallagher: I’m okay committing to p95 15 min for Hosted/Dedicated as an internal target; externally we phrase as “rollback executable within minutes” + “operational playbooks.”

Allison Grant: We’ll need default dashboards to back this up:
- timeline of config versions
- overlay with p95 latency/error rate
- propagation progress
- “last known good version” marker

Aisha Bello: + add error budget consumption panel for routes (helps decide if we rollback vs wait).

Devon Price: If you all agree on thresholds, I can wire alert templates so incident-bot posts “Rollback to vX (last known good)” and includes the config_change_id.

Sean Gallagher: Action items:
1) Allison/Aisha: confirm metric + label standards (env, mode, customer_id hashed?, scope_id, config_change_id).
2) Devon: draft incident-bot message template + required fields.
3) Rafael/Tomáš: runbook requirements—what must be shown in Console to safely rollback.

I’ll summarize here once we converge.

deploy-bot: (internal) Reminder: Proposed alert rules should be added to observability-pack repo (grafana/alerts) and reviewed by #eng-observability before enabling in prod.

Neha Kapoor: :thumbsup: on the SLO split by Hosted/Dedicated/Private and the two-stage stuck alert.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: Please make sure the page includes: customer + region + scope + “current live version” + “target version” + deep link to rollback.

Allison Grant: 👍 I’ll propose label redaction rules too (customer identifiers). Security will want this.

Sean Gallagher: Cool. I’ll post a cleaned-up SLO/alert spec in Confluence after this thread, but this is the baseline for Phase 1 acceptance criteria.
